title: Quantitative supported Tor bounds and their uniform integral restriction
statement:
Fix a field $k$, a prime $\ell$ invertible in $k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $k$ with closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the actual finite and derived-complete integral categories $D^b_c(T,A_n)$ and $D^b_c(T,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], ordinary finite derived tensor and integral derived reduction [def-weil-derived-tensor, def-weil-integral-derived-reduction].
Suppose the specified $i_*,i^*,j^*,Rj_*,J$ preserve these constructible categories, with $i_*\dashv J$, invertible $i^*i_*\to1$, and supported distinguished triangles $i_*JK\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to$. Assume canonical reductions identify each integral operation with its finite counterpart, preserving both adjunction maps; for $J$ this includes $(JK)_n\cong J_nK_n$. Let $N\ge0$ be independent of $n$. Suppose at every finite level $i_*,i^*,j^*$ preserve Tor intervals unchanged and $Rj_*$ sends Tor interval $[a,b]$ into $[a,b+N]$, with the all-module-sheaf meaning [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Then $J_n$ sends Tor interval $[a,b]$ into $[a,b+N+1]$. More precisely, for $\kappa=A_n/(\varpi)$ and every $K$ of interval $[a,b]$, both $i_*J_nK\otimes^L_{A_n}\kappa$ and $J_nK\otimes^L_{A_n}\kappa$ have cohomology only in $[a,b+N+1]$.
At integral coefficients $i_*,i^*,j^*$ preserve the uniform Tor interval of the reductions; $Rj_*$ and $J$ send it respectively into $[a,b+N]$ and $[a,b+N+1]$. The supported triangles and adjunctions consequently restrict to the full triangulated categories $D^b_{ctf}$, and any vanishing $JRj_*=0$ and invertible unit $1\to Ji_*$ on $D^b_c$ restrict there too. At the field stages $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ this restriction is the identity since $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ by definition.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$, put $A=A_n$, $F=i_*J_nK$ and $C=Rj_*j^*K$. The assumed interval preservation gives $j^*K$ interval $[a,b]$ and $C$ interval $[a,b+N]$. Both are bounded constructible by hypothesis, hence finite-Tor objects by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. By the shift formula in [lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated], $C[-1]$ has interval $[a+1,b+N+1]$.

source.place: Finite Tor amplitude: clause (2 prime) and Other stages; returned steps 18–19

proof.text: Inverse rotation of the assumed distinguished triangle $F\to K\to C\to F[1]$ gives a distinguished triangle $C[-1]\to F\to K\to C$ by [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Enlarge the two outside Tor intervals to $[a,b+N+1]$ directly in their all-module vanishing predicates. This is allowed since $N\geq0$. Apply the common-interval extension clause of [lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated]. Thus $F=i_*J_nK$ has the asserted interval, without changing site presentations or using a residue criterion.

source.place: Finite Tor amplitude: clause (2 prime) and Other stages; returned steps 18–19

proof.text: Apply the assumed interval-preserving $i^*$ to $F$. The assumed isomorphism $i^*i_*\cong1$ identifies $i^*F$ with $J_nK$, so $J_nK$ also has interval $[a,b+N+1]$. Tor bounds are invariant under isomorphism, since tensor and cohomology are functors. In the all-module definition [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], take the degree-zero constant module $\kappa=A_n/(\varpi)$ on $X$ and on $Z$. This gives exactly the two asserted residue-tensor cohomological bounds.

source.place: Finite Tor amplitude: clause (2 prime) and Other stages; returned steps 18–19

proof.text: Let an integral object have reductions with a single Tor interval $[a,b]$. For each $n$, use the assumed canonical comparison $(TK)_n\cong T_nK_n$ separately for $T=i_*,i^*,j^*,Rj_*,J$. The finite hypotheses and steps 1–3 give respectively $[a,b]$, $[a,b]$, $[a,b]$, $[a,b+N]$, $[a,b+N+1]$ for these reductions. These same intervals work for every $n$, because $N$ is independent of $n$. Each integral output already belongs to $D^b_c$ by hypothesis. Thus these are uniform Tor bounds in exactly the integral definition [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]; no inverse-limit cohomological bound is inferred.

source.place: Finite Tor amplitude: clause (2 prime) and Other stages; returned steps 18–19

proof.text: At finite levels use the isomorphism-closure and triangulation clauses of [lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated]. For integral coefficients intersect the triangulated constructible predicate of [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated] with the uniform Tor predicate of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The scalar reduction construction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] supplies a shift comparison and exact triangulated structure at every level. Isomorphisms preserve intervals by composing cochain-representative isomorphisms. For zero, obtain an interval for each reduction from finite triangulation and shift its zero object until the upper bound is below any test degree; hence $[0,0]$ works at every level. Shifts have the common interval $[a-m,b-m]$ by the finite quantitative shift clause. Reduce an integral triangle, enlarge its outside intervals to their common minimum/maximum interval, and apply the finite common-interval extension clause. These closure properties give the full triangulated subcategory by [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory].

source.place: Finite Tor amplitude: clause (2 prime) and Other stages; returned steps 18–19

proof.text: All vertices of each supported triangle on a finite-Tor input now lie in the finite-Tor subcategory, by steps 1–4; its triangle is distinguished there by the inherited-triangle description in [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. Fullness identifies each restricted Hom set with its ambient Hom set. The given adjunction bijections therefore restrict, naturally, to these Hom sets; the same ambient units and counits satisfy the same identities. Any assumed zero functor $JRj_*$ and isomorphism $1\to Ji_*$ remain zero and invertible on these objects (an inverse is an arrow in the full subcategory). Finally [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] defines $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ at $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, so at either field stage the restriction is the identity.
